boracite.identity: IMA September2026 p28: Boracite, Mg3B7O13Cl, G, 1789; page1 defines grandfathered status and original-description year. Not a sequential IMA approval identifier.
boracite.accepted: Burns and Carpenter1996 original pp881-892. Only natural Mg-rich EB/S4A/S4B belong to this owner. Optical Pca21/F-43c transitions and powder cell-volume discontinuities support a laboratory solid-state transformation, not extraction.
locators: Table2 p884 composition and calculated B2O3
Tables4-5 and Figure3 EB/S4A diffraction series
pp888-889 volume strain and model limits
boracite.conditions: EB from England, exact locality unknown; S4A/S4B CMN F93-20-4 from New Brunswick evaporites. Warm-water halite removal is preparation. Optical approximately30-micrometre sections, Linkam stage calibration plus/minus2C; powder ground+Si onPt strip, plus/minus10C calibration, approximately3h scans. Heating rate/atmosphere not specified.
boracite.measurements: Table3 EB272+/-5C, S4A287+/-3C, S4B283+/-2C: onset-to-completion ranges, not replicate errors. Approximate cubic-to-orthorhombic cell-volume increases0.12%EB and0.06%S4A. Synthetic-endmember264C is a prior-study value and excluded from new observations.
limits: B2O3 calculated from stoichiometry; Fe+Mn+Mg normalized3. EB analytical total105.39wt% not silently normalized.
Cubic cell constraints applied even to low-symmetry powder data; no new atomic-coordinate refinement.
Landau model alternatives not distinguished by precision; Fe-rich continuity trend does not fully agree with optical evidence. No transfer of Fe-rich congolite/trembathite outcomes.
1996 article DOI not established; separate1997 infrared follow-up discovered but not acquired or used.
boracite.visuals: All12 original pages, allTables1-6 andFigures1-5 inspected. IMA pages1 and28 inspected.

larderellite.identity: IMA September2026 p121: Larderellite, (NH4)B5O7(OH)2·H2O, G,1854. Ideal formula follows current authority rather than the missing-parentheses typography of Table1.
larderellite.accepted: Fastelli et al2020 DOI10.3390/min10100902, complete22-page version2 journalPDF from institutional repository. Mixed natural Larderello sample characterized by diffraction and separate TG/DSC; accept qualitative mass-loss transformation with qualified author interpretation.
locators: sections2.2-2.3 pp4-5 diffraction and thermal methods
larderellite.conditions: Starting fit94.3%larderellite,0.4%bassanite,5.3%polyhalite. TG approximately20mg NetzschSTA490, separateDSC approximately3mg MettlerToledo;10C/min andair50mL/min. Figure2b extends TG approximately1023K andDSC773K. No evolved-gas analysis or replicate uncertainty reported.
limits: Prose32.5%totalmassloss conflicts with visualFigure2b endpoint approximately72-73%massremaining. Visual estimate is not digitized raw data or a corrected yield.
Six-major-step assertion enumerates eight temperatures. Individual H2O/NH3 losses are inferred assignments, not measured evolved gases; no gas yields adopted.

Prior phase/product sequence onp7 is attributed to Waclawska1997; original not acquired. PDFreference58 hyperlinks DOI10.1016/S0925-8388(97)00036-4, but attempted live resolution failed; retain as a reference-derived lead. Do not adopt BO3/B2O3 phase identity.
Reflectance methods/abstract use293/193K while some figure/results labels use298/198K. No numerical spectral temperatures/band assignments adopted.
Cooling-cycle diffraction is not evidence of a heated-residue product refinement. No pure-mineral recovery/industrial/microbial claim.
